video.readability.evidence: [audience·claude] I watched the contact sheet as a first-time viewer, and the cause-and-effect chain is readable. 0–1.75s: a large scorpion is on the left and three tree/moss golems are on the right, moving toward it. 2.0–5.75s: the golems get close and there's some melee with flying debris. 6.0–6.25s: the scorpion raises its tail and arcs it over the nearest golem. 6.5–7.75s: a bright green poison glow appears on that golem's chest, which reads as the scorpion stinging it with poison. 8.0–9.0s: the green glow spreads through the golem, and it falls and lies flat on the ground. 9.25–9.75s: a large yellow-green poison cloud bursts out of the fallen golem. 10.0–11.0s: the other two golems turn dark brown and look scorched. 11.25–11.75s: they collapse. 12.0–13.75s: the scorpion is the only one left standing, and the three golems are smoking, charred heaps on the ground. My summary: the scorpion stung one tree golem with a poison tail strike, the poison exploded into a gas cloud, and all three golems died. The scorpion wins. Two weak spots, neither enough to block my reading: in 2.0–5.75s the golems and the scorpion overlap so much it's hard to tell who is hitting whom, and the sting's green light at 6.5–7.0s is small and partly blocked by the golem's body.
